status: Referred to House Emerging Issues Committee 2026-05-15 (last recorded action, the day of constitutional adjournment); no hearing was ever scheduled and no committee action followed; died without further action at sine die, 2026-05-15
key_provisions: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Environmental Accountability Act. Applies to AI-optimized data centers with 100 MW or greater IT load and major expansions; requires closed-loop or equivalent cooling, annual environmental and health reports, water and air monitoring, public health complaint reporting, and penalties.

status: Public Hearing Completed in House Conservation and Natural Resources Committee 2026-03-30 (last recorded action); no committee vote, Do Pass report, or calendar placement followed; died without further action at sine die, 2026-05-15
key_provisions: Creates new provisions for industrial utility users. Press release describes the bill as requiring large-load electricity consumers, including data centers, to pay costs for grid expansions, new generating capacity, or infrastructure upgrades; also creates water-resource protections.

status: Referred to House Emerging Issues Committee 2026-05-15 (last recorded action, the day of constitutional adjournment); no hearing was ever scheduled and no committee action followed; died without further action at sine die, 2026-05-15
key_provisions: One-year St. Louis data center permitting pause. Would pause acceptance, processing, or approval of applications allowing creation or expansion of data centers until 2027-08-28 in a city not within a county; applications submitted before 2026-08-28 would be exempt.

status: Referred to House Emerging Issues Committee 2026-05-15 (last recorded action, the day of constitutional adjournment); no hearing was ever scheduled and no committee action followed; died without further action at sine die, 2026-05-15
key_provisions: Creates hyperscale data center siting restrictions. Defines hyperscale at 25 MW or more; prohibits hyperscale data centers in specified land use categories and agricultural zoning in unincorporated areas; adds 500-foot setback/native planting barrier, noise-control, local approval, ratepayer cost-shift, incentive affidavit, and major industrial water-user permit provisions.

status: Second Read and Referred to Senate Transportation, Infrastructure and Public Safety Committee 2026-05-07 (last recorded action, 8 days before adjournment); no hearing was scheduled; died without further action at sine die, 2026-05-15
key_provisions: Creates provisions relating to the regulation of large load electric customers. Lowers the Public Service Commission tariff-filing threshold for large electrical corporations (over 250,000 customers) from 100 MW to 50 MW of projected annual peak demand (Section 393.130.7). New Section 393.325 requires an owner/operator of a 'large load facility' (a category that includes data centers) intending to operate after 2026-08-28 to file a disclosure of intent with the PSC before signing utility contracts, undergo PSC-reviewed pre- and post-construction studies, bear its own infrastructure costs without shifting them to other ratepayers in general rate cases, contribute to low-income ratepayer assistance programs once operational, and implement an emergency curtailment system (with exemptions for hospitals, long-term care, and first-responder facilities).

status: Enacted; Truly Agreed To and Finally Passed 2025-03-13; signed by Governor 2025-04-09 (Senate Journal p. S788); effective 2025-08-28; no repeal or amendment identified as of 2026-07-31
key_provisions: Utility law requiring large-load tariff filings. Missouri PSC later approved Ameren Missouri's large-load plan for customers needing 75 MW or more of monthly peak demand, including data centers, with customer-protection terms.
